item.content:encoded:
The attention to investigative procedure and the interesting, but not too OTT Foundation tech really set a nice tone to the story. I like the anomaly in the story as well. Something uncanny and strange, but quietly beautiful, acting as a good setting that serves to further characterization of the two main characters, and also a fascinating thing in its own right. The mood achieved by the unique nature of the museum suited the story perfectly.

This piece is a very good example of a writer developing their own voice and style, in a way that's in service to getting a story out there, rather than being idiosyncratic for its own sake. Unmistakeably of the author, but not self-absorbed. This is very good work.

item.title: Author Notes
item.content:encoded:
Many thanks to Dr Reach and Zolgamax for asking lots of questions during chat review, and to Wogglebug for pointing out word choice and other details, and to Loiterer, Djoric, vezaz, djkaktus, tahunu, and TwistedGears and for reading it over in chat. Let me know if there’s anyone else I forgot to mention…

Anyway, why bird figurines? I like birds. I have a pair of blown-glass tiny bird figurines myself. They’re adorable. Might make them into an SCP one day. Also, there was this adorable frosted glass bluebird I once saw on sale in a museum gift shop—it was gorgeous, and small enough to fit in my palm. It was also eighty dollars. Oof. Didn’t buy it, but took a picture and remembered it.

About the museum itself…

Potential spoilers
hide

Regarding the whole “things taken out of the museum start to go melty, and when put back start to make other things deform” bit… what else do we know holds memories and exhibits similar behavior if you take bits out? Same goes for the lights. Lights run on electricity. What else operates using electrical signals?

And why crystal? Well, for one, it’s pretty… and it’s a bit of a stretch, but ever heard of Spearman’s g and crystallized intelligence?

I like museums. I like listening to people who talk while they walk around museums. I remember some interesting snippets. I wonder who else, and what else, also remembers such things.
